key_insight: MedRLM reframes clinical AI as a recursive, multimodal reasoning system that can inspect, verify, and synthesize long patient histories instead of answering isolated questions.
clinical_relevance: It could improve decision support for complex cases by linking EHRs, images, sensor streams, guidelines, and referral rules into a more auditable workflow.
method: Uses specialized agents for clinical text, longitudinal EHR, medical imaging, physiological sensors, guideline retrieval, uncertainty auditing, and referral planning.
Builds a Clinical Evidence Graph Memory to connect patient observations with retrieved evidence, biomarker definitions, and referral criteria.
Triggers deeper reasoning when abnormal sensor patterns or low-confidence outputs suggest higher risk.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes an evaluation plan using public and credentialed datasets spanning EHR, radiology, ECG, ICU time series, and referral-proxy outcomes.
watch_item: Performance may depend on data quality, interoperability, and careful clinician oversight because recursive multimodal pipelines can still propagate errors across sources.
paper_title: MedRLM: Recursive Multimodal Health Intelligence for Long-Context Clinical Reasoning, Sensor-Guided Screening, Evidence-Grounded Decision Support, and Community-to-Tertiary Referral Optimization
